long_biography.plain_text:
Altec began as the Alabama Truck Equipment Company, a small business created by Lee Styslinger III’s grandfather during the Depression. His father took control after the founder’s early death and developed it into a manufacturer of equipment for electric utilities and telecommunications companies. Styslinger entered that established family enterprise after completing his undergraduate degree, then added a Harvard MBA while building his career inside the business.

He rose to president and then chief executive. During twenty-four years at the helm, Altec combined manufacturing with rental, finance, parts and service operations and reached customers around the world. A formal succession in 2021 transferred the chief executive role to a non-family leader. Styslinger and his brothers retained oversight through the ownership council, and he continued as co-chairman through 2024.
